newsitem.title: GREECE: ING BARINGS IS BULLISH ON GREEK EQUITIES.
newsitem.headline: ING BARINGS IS BULLISH ON GREEK EQUITIES.

text.p: The Athens bourse rally is just the beginning of a longer-term climb but investors should pick quality stocks with high earnings growth rather than laggards, said ING Barings in a flash report on Wednesday.

"If this is the beginning of a longer term rally, as we believe it is, then investors should focus more on quality and earnings growth and less on which stocks have been left behind," said ING Barings.
Most laggard stocks were fairly priced in terms of fundamental valuations but some like fast food chain Goody's, cosmetics firm Sarantis and construction firms GEK and Edrasi were oversold.
Alpha Credit Bank , Hellenic Bottling and Titan Cement would continue to rally.

"Among the better quality stocks that were deservedly left-behind are: Ergo Bank , Heracles Cement , National Bank , Delta Dairy and Attica Enterprises," analyst Yannis Protopapadakis said in the report titled "Is it finally happening?".

The main reason for the recent rally was the bourse's failure to absorb good news in 1996 such as a more stable political environment, a new government committed to reforms whose credibility was enhanced by not bowing to farmers' demands and falling inflation and interest rates.

Foreign and local retail investors were the buyers behind the recent rally responding to top-down improvements during end-year country allocations and portfolio reshuffling on the back of falling yields on Greek government securities. --Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
